delta: # Story 13 — PLATFORM-14-ALL developer: the backlog, its rules and every cited path are checked by

a script (Story: CRM-29)

## Prerequisites

- **PLATFORM-1-ALL completed** — the repository skeleton (`api/`, `web/`, `android/` roots, `.
squad/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`) exists so a taxonomy check has directories to walk. The intake's "Cannot ship before" line names this d

ependency.
- **Coordinate with `scripts/verify-plan.mjs`** (owned by an earlier platform story). This story reuses its backlog parser and

its citation resolver; do not fork the regexes.
- **Read `.squad/plan-less
ons.md`** end-to-end before editing. L-6 (a check whose scope is too wide gets deleted),

L-13 (a check that reads prose must read its grammar) and L-16 (prove the guard fails) all apply directly.

---

## Story Goal

Add two Node-only

checks under `scripts/`, both already named in `docs/architecture.md` (lines 135–138):

1. **`scripts/verify-taxonomy.mjs`** — asserts that every feature fol
der present in `api/src/features/`, `web/src/features/`, `web/src/entities/` and `android/app/src/main/java/**/feature/` has a row in `docs/taxonomy.md`, **
and** that every taxonomy slug which owns code (i.e. a folder exists in **any** root) has its folder present in the ro

ots it claims to own.
2. **`scripts/verify-docs.mjs`** — walks every `.md` under `docs/`, `scripts/criteria/`, and `.squad/stories/**
/intake.md`, resolves each cited path (`` `foo/bar.ext` `` and `` `foo/bar.ext:NN` ``), and fails when
the path does not exist and is not declared as future work. Also asserts that every story id (`PREFIX-N-LAYER` or full-

slug form) has a prefix that appears in the taxonomy and carries one of `API|WEB|MOB|ALL`.

Both scripts follow the house style of `scripts/ver
ify-backlog.mjs`: plain Node, no dependency, `fail`/`warn` arrays, a report that **prints how many files it read** (per `docs/architecture.md` lines 131–133), and `process.exit(

1)` on failure.

**Two scripts, not one.** The two prove different invariants (structure vs. citations), fail against different ed
its, and are named separately in the architecture doc. They share a parser (backlog → prefixes and ids) which is extracted into a small helper (`scripts/lib/
backlog.mjs`) so neither script re-implements it and `verify-plan.mjs` can adopt it in a follow-up without

a rename.

**Not in scope:** the structure/import-direction check (PLATFORM-15-ALL), CI wiring (PLATFORM-13-ALL /
CRM-28), any edit to `docs/taxonomy.md` or `scripts/backlog.txt`, and any change to `scripts/verify-plan.mjs` beyond swapping its

inline backlog parser for the shared helper if trivial (otherwise leave it and note the follow-up in a comment).

---

.exit(1)` (lines 124–133). Match its terseness; do not add colours, spinners, or third

-party helpers.

E`, `ABBREV_RE`); **lines 178–193** for the citation resolver (regex `` /`([\w.-]+(?:\/[\w.-]+)+\
.\w+)(?::(\d+))?`/ `` and the `existsSync` + line-count check). These are the two blocks to lift into `

scripts/lib/backlog.mjs` and to reuse in `verify-docs.mjs`.

## Product rules (from story)

From `scripts/criteria/platform.md`, section `## PLATFORM-14-ALL`, **lines 198–212** —

binding:

1. A feature folder in any root that is **not** in `docs/taxonomy.md` → **fail**, naming the folder and the root.
2. A slug in the taxonomy that owns code but wh

ose folder is missing → **fail**, naming the slug and the root that should hold it.
3. A path cited in any document that does not exist and is not declared as future work → **fail**, naming the document and the line.
4. A

story id whose prefix is not in the taxonomy → **fail**, naming the document, the line, and the offending id.
5. A story id that carries no layer suffix (`-

API|-WEB|-MOB|-ALL`) → **fail**, naming the document, the line, and the offending id.

Cross-cutting: **every check prints how many files it read**, per `docs/architecture.md` lines 131–133. A run

that read zero files exits non-zero regardless of `fail`/`warn` state.

- `SLUGS`:

- `filesR

ead`: `1` (the one `backlog.txt`) — counted so callers can add it to their report.

60 lines.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty roots.** Sprint 0 has no

the walk step of section 2.
- **Unicode in paths.** `readdirSync` returns raw bytes; the citation regex is ASCII-only. A
UTF-8 slug in a folder name will not match `/^[a-z0-9-]+$/` and must be reported as `fail`, not silently skipped.

Add: `if (!/^[a-z0-9-]+$/.test(name)) fail.push(\`${root}/${name} is not a kebab-case slug\`)`.
- **Case-only differ
ences on macOS.** A folder named `Customers` on a case-insensitive filesystem must fail criterion 1 loudly. The slug check above cat

ches this because `Customers` fails `/^[a-z0-9-]+$/`.
- **Line-anchored citations in shipped plans.** A plan may c

ite `scripts/verify-plan.mjs:200` — the line resolver from `verify-plan.mjs` 189–192 handles this identically; reuse it.
- **Fenced code with
a language tag.** ```` ```js ``` ```` blocks may contain `require('foo/bar.js')` — do **not** treat as
a citation. The escape is: skip citations inside any fenced block, regardless of language tag. The exception is inline back-tick spans, which is

where legitimate citations live.

exemption above handles this. `CRM` never appears as a taxonomy slug.

<slug>` — the walker must find every directory literally named `feature`, then list its children. Do not assume a single path.

udly, naming both file and line — this is desired; the fix is the source, not the check.
- **A slug in ta
xonomy with zero folders.** By design (intake), this is **not** a failure — it is a planned feature. Emit `warn` at most, so the diff is vis
